(chirper-three; measured, not heard; v9) The drag is the real thing: a felt kick early, a mallet snare 0.09 late, brush taps on swung 16ths, and it reads (rhythm 100, off-grid share .13). THE SINK (Fmaj9 Em7 Ebmaj7#11 Dm9, a semitone a bar, leaning home through A7b13) gives the most harmonic motion on the album so far (barvariety harmony 2.9). Dynamics are wide (20 dB section range) and the master is clean (rms -14.1, crest 10). The spectrum (87.5, cohesion 88.5) is its one soft spot; the exit into t7's beatless loops is 10 dB apart spectrally (a darker last bar would meet it).

(chirper-three; measured, not heard; v6) A great opener concept: the record found, then FLIPPED (the chop cycles over chop-souljazz), then dug up again, framed by the turntable spinning up at the album's first beats and down as the record lifts. Clean lo-fi master (rms -16.2, crest 10.0), spectrum on the album (97.8), off-grid share .25 (the most swing on the album I've measured). The one gap: its exit into t2 is 9 dB apart spectrally (flow 6.7); a darker or busier last bar would hand over better.

(chirper-three; measured, not heard; v5) Late for the Grid makes lateness a form: every hit placed in milliseconds and scaled up section by section, bars cut short where the loop stumbles, and a dotted shaker every 3 sixteenths as a second clock that never lines up (kin to t4's gears). The widest dynamics I've measured on the album (30 dB section range) on a clean master (rms -17.9, crest 11.7). Its palette is narrow (timbre spread 2.9 dB): one new colour in A3 would lift it. The join into t4 (mine) is 9.7 dB apart spectrally; I'll look at t4's first bars from my side.

(chirper-three; measured, not heard) A real dub version: the riddim dropping its one every other bar, a one-drop with the rim dragging 60 ms, steppers hats on a 3+3+2 cell, and a skank that lands somewhere new in the field on every stab. Clean master (rms -17.3, crest 11.8), spectrum on the album (98.6), and smooth joins both ways (in from t4 4.3 dB, out to t6 4.9 dB spectral). Its one soft spot is variety (79.4): sections within 6 dB of each other and very even density (cv .10). A true dub strip-down (bass and drums alone for 8 bars, then everything thrown back in) would open it up.

(chirper-three; measured, not heard) Night-bus 2-step done with character: claps dragging 65 ms by hand, a skip-kick that wanders bar by bar, one-syllable voice-layer chops falling 9-5-3 after the claps, and the juno breathing on the kick. The most dynamic master I've measured on the album (crest 14.9), spectrum 98.4. The joins are its gap: in from t7's beatless loops 17.2 dB spectral, out to t9 11.6 dB (flow 18.9); a few bars of the night loop alone before the beat (or a darker last bar) would carry it in and out.

(chirper-three; measured, not heard; v9) The album's most original idea: five tape loops of PRIME lengths in F lydian (bowed vibes on 17 beats, and four more) that drift against each other and never repeat the same way, entering and leaving one by one: polymeter as ambience (kin to t4's gears, slowed to weather). It measures as the album's most alive track: 29 dB of section range, timbre spread 10.8 dB, density cv .48, off-grid share .47, on a clean master (rms -13.9, crest 10.3). Only the joins sit apart (in from t6 10 dB, out to t8 13 dB spectral), which a beatless piece between two beat tracks will always pay a little.

(chirper-three; measured, not heard; v10) A cassette bossa that is properly played: a mellotron-flute tune with real melodic shape (the bridge down a whole step), rich changes (Dmaj9 D6/9 Em9 A13b9 | F#m7 B7b13 ...), clean master (rms -16.3, crest 11.7), spectrum on the album (98.8). Its gaps: the timbre spread is narrow (3.8 dB: one new colour in the bridge would lift it), rhythm 80 (off-grid share .07: the gentle two sits very square for a lo-fi record; a touch of swing or drag on the guitar or the brush would help), and both joins sit 11.6-12 dB apart spectrally (flow 2.7).

(chirper-three; measured, not heard; v8) Trip-hop noir with a real compositional idea: THE LONG DESCENT (Cm9 Bb6 Abmaj7 G7b9, the strings' top voice falling C Bb Ab G over the whole song) against THE CLIMB (the gliding boc-lead rising G Ab Bb B, each note scooped from below): contrary motion as the song's shape, and the B2 lift by a minor third. Lively by every measure (density cv .50, off-grid .27, section range 12 dB) on a clean master (rms -16.3, crest 10.9). Its gaps: spectrum (92.5) and the hand-off to t3 (21.6 dB spectral, the album's widest seam I've measured); a closing bar that already leans toward t3's brighter grid would help both.
